title: Beyond Integrability Preserving Renormalization-Group Protocol in Non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with Time-Dependent Interaction Strengths
abstract: It is well established that in time-dependent quantum systems, integrability preserving time-dependent interaction strengths are identical to the renormalization group (RG) trajectories of the corresponding static model when time `$t$' in the driven model is identified with the logarithm of the cutoff `$\logΛ$' of the static model. We refer to this integrability preserving driving as the RG protocol. In this work we extend the class of time-dependent integrable models to include non-Hermitian quantum models with time-dependent interaction strengths. Using the recently formulated generalized Bethe ansatz framework [P. R. Pasnoori, Phys. Rev. B 112, L060409 (2025)], we show that the constraints imposed by integrability are more general: The interaction strengths of the static model that flow in the RG follow the respective RG trajectories in the corresponding time-dependent model as described above. In addition, the interaction strengths of the static model that are RG invariant can either be constant or have a specific time-dependence in the corresponding time-dependent model which is constrained by integrability. Thus we establish that in the context of time-dependent non-Hermitian systems, the set of integrability preserving time-dependent strengths is larger than the set corresponding to the RG protocol.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how integrability constrains time-dependent quantum systems, specifically extending the analysis to non-Hermitian Hamiltonians. By using the generalized Bethe ansatz, the authors prove that the constraints are more general than the standard Renormalization Group (RG) protocol. This reveals new, non-RG-predicted dynamical pathways for the system's coupling strengths.
main_problem: The paper extends the study of integrability-preserving time-dependent quantum models to non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, comparing the constraints imposed by integrability against the standard Renormalization Group (RG) protocol.
main_result: The set of integrability-preserving time-dependent strengths is shown to be larger than those predicted by the RG protocol, allowing for time evolutions that trace perfect limit cycles in the coupling parameter space.
method: The analysis utilizes the generalized Bethe ansatz framework to derive consistency conditions (Yang-Baxter equations) for the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
model_or_system: The primary model is the time-dependent non-Hermitian Kondo model, characterized by a time-dependent complex interaction strength J(t). The static counterpart involves analyzing RG flow in the Kondo model, which exhibits distinct phases (Kondo, YSR, local moment).
key_observables: The time evolution of the inverse interaction strength, 1/J(t), and the parameters defining the phase space trajectories (limit cycles).
important_parameters: The time-dependent coupling strength J(t), the RG invariant parameter $f_i$, and the rate of time dependence in $1/J(t)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the consistency conditions derived from the generalized Bethe ansatz structure, and the comparison is made by allowing complex time-dependent coupling strengths.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the three phases of the static model with RG flow trajectories. Figure 2 shows the phase space plot of Im(J) vs Re(J), contrasting the standard RG flow with the newly found limit cycles for the non-Hermitian case.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the background of the RG protocol in integrable systems. It then applies the generalized Bethe ansatz to the non-Hermitian time-dependent model, deriving constraints that lead to linear time dependence for 1/J(t). Finally, it compares these constraints to the RG flow, demonstrating the larger set of integrable paths.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful generalization of integrability concepts from Hermitian to non-Hermitian systems, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems and non-equilibrium dynamics where non-Hermiticity is common.
